title: Ada and the Cipher
premise: Coral Quintana's photographic memory has made him the town of Ada's unofficial archivist—until a drowned man surfaces wearing Coral's own missing clothes, staged to frame him. As Coral investigates, he realizes the killer is someone who once shared his life: Ada, the foster sister who vanished years ago, leaving behind a coded notebook he's never been able to crack. Ada is killing the people who covered up the fire that destroyed their childhood group home, and Coral must decode her cipher and choose between exposing her and protecting the fragile family they've rebuilt—ending with Coral turning the cipher over to the police, Ada surrendering rather than letting him take the fall, and Coral learning that memory kept secret is just another kind of prison.
about_author: O. M. Almeida is the pen name of a former insurance fraud analyst who spent a decade reading other people's disasters for a living. Almeida writes mysteries about people whose careful, ordered lives are cracked open by the past they thought they'd filed away.

chapters.title: Alphabetical Order
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Establishes his photographic memory, his methodical life in Ada, and his habit of filing the town's secrets. He notices his closet has been disturbed—nothing stolen, everything shifted one hanger. Emotional beat: the unease of a man whose perfect system has been touched.

chapters.title: The Drowned File
chapters.summary: A body surfaces in the reservoir wearing Coral's missing clothes, including his distinctive monogrammed jacket. The sheriff, an old friend, quietly warns him he's a suspect. Coral memorizes every detail of the scene, cataloging what doesn't fit. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into focus.

chapters.title: Everyone's Alibi, Nobody's Truth
chapters.summary: Coral interviews the victim's acquaintances under the pretext of a life-insurance claim. His memory catches three contradictory timelines no one else notices. A stranger with familiar eyes watches him from across the diner. Emotional beat: the loneliness of seeing what others hide.

chapters.title: What the Fire Took
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: twelve-year-old Coral and his foster sister Ada survive the Hillcrest group home fire that killed their caretaker. Present-day Coral realizes the victim was the fire inspector who declared it an accident. Emotional beat: grief he'd filed away breaking open.

chapters.title: The Notebook in the Wall
chapters.summary: Coral retrieves Ada's childhood cipher notebook from the ruins of Hillcrest, which he's secretly visited for years. The cipher is one they invented together—half of it is in her head, half in his. Emotional beat: hope that she's alive, dread of why she'd return.

chapters.title: Second Body, Same Jacket Size
chapters.summary: A retired social worker is found dead, again staged with Coral's belongings—this time his car keys. The sheriff can no longer protect him. Coral realizes the killer is building a case against him, item by item. Emotional beat: the trap tightening.

chapters.title: The Town That Keeps Secrets
chapters.summary: Coral uses his archive of the town's secrets to identify the Hillcrest cover-up's players: the inspector, the social worker, the contractor who cut the fire code, the judge who sealed the records. Emotional beat: his gift as a weapon finally turned outward.

chapters.title: Cipher Half-Remembered
chapters.summary: Working nights, Coral cracks the first layer of Ada's notebook: a list of names, each crossed out in a different hand. Two are already dead. He decodes a warning addressed to him by childhood nickname. Emotional beat: she's been leaving him messages for years.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: A witness places Coral near the reservoir the night of the first murder—impossible, since Coral was home, and he can prove it, but only to himself. His alibi is his memory, and no one trusts that anymore. Emotional beat: his greatest gift becoming his greatest liability.

chapters.title: Marisol
chapters.summary: Coral's neighbor and only friend, Marisol, a diner cook who took him in after the fire, confronts him about his midnight absences. He lies badly. She reveals she knew about Hillcrest all along and chose to let him forget. Emotional beat: found family strained by protective silence.

chapters.title: The Contractor's Confession
chapters.summary: Coral confronts the contractor, who confesses on tape to falsifying the Hillcrest inspection for the judge's brother. Hours later, the contractor is found dead—and the recording is gone, along with Coral's recorder. Emotional beat: every move he makes feeds the frame.

chapters.title: Arrest Warrant
chapters.summary: The sheriff, cornered by evidence, must bring Coral in. In the interrogation room, Coral reconstructs the entire case from memory, exposing holes the detectives missed. He's released on a technicality he himself pointed out. Emotional beat: humiliation transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Judge's Sealed Room
chapters.summary: Coral breaks into the judge's office and finds the sealed Hillcrest file—and a copy of Ada's cipher, meaning the judge has known Ada survived. The judge is found dead the next morning, the fourth name crossed out. Emotional beat: he's racing a list, not a person.

chapters.title: One Name Left
chapters.summary: Decoding deeper, Coral finds the final name on Ada's list isn't the judge—it's Marisol, who signed the report placing the children back at Hillcrest the week of the fire. Coral refuses to believe Ada would hurt her. Emotional beat: loyalty at war with evidence.

chapters.title: The Reservoir at Night
chapters.summary: Coral stakes out the reservoir and finally sees her: Ada, older, scarred, alive. She doesn't run. She tells him the fire wasn't an accident—the caretaker was killed, and the cover-up buried it with them inside. Emotional beat: reunion and betrayal in the same breath.

chapters.title: Sister
chapters.summary: Ada's account: the caretaker abused the children, died in a struggle the night of the fire, and the adults conspired to call it accidental with the children trapped inside. Ada survived; Coral was pulled out and remembers nothing. Emotional beat: his memory's one blind spot explained.

chapters.title: The Fifth Name
chapters.summary: Coral decodes the notebook's final layer: Ada's list has a fifth name, uncrossed—Coral himself. Not as a target, but as her intended final witness: she staged the frame to force him to remember Hillcrest. Emotional beat: the horror that he was the plan all along.

chapters.title: What Coral Forgot
chapters.summary: Under Ada's prompting at the Hillcrest ruins, Coral's memory unlocks: he saw the caretaker's death, and Marisol helped him bury it to protect him. Marisol arrives at the ruins, having followed him. Emotional beat: the price of survival—everyone protected him into complicity.

chapters.title: Three at the Ruins
chapters.summary: Marisol confesses her role; Ada raises the crowbar she's kept for years, ready to finish her list. Coral steps between them, offering the one thing Ada never had: someone who remembers her as she was, not as what the fire made. Emotional beat: the standoff as family reckoning.

chapters.title: The Cipher Turned Over
chapters.summary: Sirens approach—Marisol called the sheriff before following Coral. Ada nearly flees, but Coral hands her the notebook and tells her the truth deserves her name on it, not his silence. She surrenders. Emotional beat: choosing accountability over escape.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Coral testifies, reconstructing the Hillcrest conspiracy from pure memory; the surviving conspirators are charged, and Ada's sentence is tempered by the abuse documented in her cipher. Marisol stands by him in the courtroom. Emotional beat: memory as justice, finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: What He Keeps
chapters.summary: Months later, Coral visits Ada in prison, bringing her a new notebook—blank pages this time, for the future instead of the past. He rehangs his clothes, leaving one gap where hers used to be. Emotional beat: found family surviving the truth, imperfect and chosen.
